learn.title: Capacity Factor Why Rated Power Is Misleading
learn.intro: A 100 MW solar farm doesn't deliver 100 MW around the clock. Capacity factor reveals the real energy output of renewables, helping engineers, investors, and policymakers compare solar, wind, and coal on equal terms for accurate grid planning.
learn.c1_text: Capacity factor measures actual electricity generated divided by the maximum possible output if a plant ran at full rated power for a whole year. A US nuclear plant averages about 93%, while onshore wind reaches roughly 35%, showing the gap between nameplate and reality.
learn.c2_title: ⚡ Why Solar and Wind Score Lower
learn.c2_text: Solar panels only produce during daylight and drop with cloud cover, while wind speeds vary seasonally. US utility-scale solar averages around 25% capacity factor. Geography matters: Arizona solar beats Germany because of stronger, more consistent sunshine year-round.
learn.c3_text: India's solar capacity factor sits near 18-20% in most states due to dust, monsoon clouds, and high temperatures that reduce panel efficiency. Rajasthan improves to 22% thanks to clearer skies. Lower factors mean India needs roughly 5 MW of solar per 1 MW of reliable coal equivalent.
learn.stat1: US nuclear capacity factor: ~93% (highest among major sources)

learn.title: Electric Buses and Trucks Explained
learn.intro: Trucks and buses cause outsized transport emissions despite being few in number. Electrifying commercial fleets cuts urban air pollution dramatically, lowers fuel costs by up to 60%, and is now accelerating globally with battery and hydrogen powertrains competing for dominance.
learn.c1_text: City buses follow fixed, short routes ideal for overnight depot charging. A typical electric bus costs about 40% more upfront but saves $100,000+ per year in diesel. Shenzhen in China has fully electrified its 16,000-bus fleet, the world's largest e-bus transition.
learn.c2_text: Long-haul trucks need massive batteries weighing up to 5 tonnes for 500 km range. Hydrogen fuel cells offer faster refueling and lighter weight for heavy freight, though green hydrogen currently costs $5-7/kg. Battery trucks dominate shorter regional hauls under 300 km.
learn.c3_text: India has electrified over 5,000 city buses under FAME-II, with Delhi targeting 80% e-bus fleet by 2025. Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Kolkata are deploying e-buses from Tata and Switch Mobility. Heavy trucking remains nascent but Tata and Ashok Leyland have begun pilot deployments.
learn.stat1: Shenzhen e-bus fleet: 16,000+ fully electric buses
learn.stat2: Electric bus fuel savings: up to $100,000+ per year per bus
learn.stat3: Long-haul truck battery weight: up to 5 tonnes for 500 km

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels Power From Both Sides
learn.intro: Bifacial solar panels capture sunlight on both front and rear surfaces, boosting output 5-30% over traditional monofacial panels. As manufacturing costs fall, bifacial modules are becoming the default choice for utility-scale solar farms worldwide, including India's largest installations.
learn.c1_text: Light reflects off ground surfaces like sand, snow, or concrete onto the panel's rear cells. Think of it like wearing a light-colored shirt that brightens your face from below in a selfie. Aluminum or white-painted ground can boost rear-side output by 20% or more.
learn.c2_text: Modern bifacial panels use n-type monocrystalline cells with transparent backsheets or dual glass. Efficiency exceeds 22% on the front side, with rear-side adding 8-15% extra. Tracking mounts that follow the sun increase bifacial gains because more light hits the back at steep angles.
learn.c3_text: India's Bhadla and Pavagadh solar parks use bifacial modules extensively. MNRE's 2022 guidelines now allow bifacial in all utility-scale tenders. With Rajasthan and Gujarat's sandy, reflective terrain, Indian bifacial projects often exceed 25% capacity factor, beating global averages.
learn.stat1: Bifacial output boost: 5-30% over monofacial panels
learn.stat3: Best bifacial projects in India exceed 25% capacity factor
learn.stat4: Global bifacial market share: over 70% of new utility solar 2024

learn.title: EV Charging Levels 1 2 and DC Fast
learn.intro: EV charging isn't one-size-fits-all. Three levels serve different needs: slow home charging, faster workplace charging, and rapid highway charging. Understanding the difference helps drivers plan trips, businesses install the right equipment, and cities build effective charging networks.
learn.c1_text: Level 1 uses a regular 120V household outlet, adding only 4-5 km of range per hour. A full charge takes 24-40 hours for typical EVs. It's essentially free since no equipment purchase is needed, perfect for hybrid owners or plug-in hybrids with small batteries under 20 kWh.
learn.c2_text: Level 2 operates at 240V like a clothes dryer, delivering 25-40 km of range per hour. A 60 kWh EV like Tata Nexon charges overnight in 7-8 hours. Home stations cost $500-1500 installed. Over 80% of US EV charging happens at Level 2 home units.
learn.c3_text: India has installed over 10,000 DC fast chargers by 2024 under FAME-II. Tata Power and Statiq operate highway corridors every 50 km on major routes. DC fast charging adds 200+ km in 30 minutes using CCS2 connectors. Bharat DC 001 standard serves smaller Indian EVs separately.

learn.stat3: DC fast charging: 200+ km in 30 minutes
learn.stat4: India DC fast chargers installed: 10,000+ by 2024

learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar puts power generation directly on homes and buildings, skipping land use entirely. India targets 40 GW of rooftop capacity by 2030, with net metering letting households export excess solar to the grid and earn credits, turning every rooftop into a mini power plant.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels on rooftops convert sunlight into DC electricity, which an inverter turns into AC power for your home. A 3 kW system needs about 200 sq ft of shadow-free roof and generates 4-5 units daily in India, covering 80-90% of an average family's needs.
learn.c2_text: Net metering means your electricity meter runs backward when you export solar to the grid. At night you import power, offsetting daytime exports. Think of the grid as a giant battery that stores your excess daytime solar for free use after sunset, saving ₹50,000+ yearly.
learn.c3_text: Launched February 2024, PM Surya Ghar Yojana offers ₹78,000 subsidy for 2 kW systems and ₹30,000 per additional kW up to 3 kW. Target: 10,000 MW residential solar. Subsidy is credited directly to bank accounts within 30 days via the national portal.

learn.title: Green Bonds and Climate Finance
learn.intro: Building renewable energy requires trillions of dollars. Green bonds channel global capital into solar, wind, and clean tech projects by offering fixed returns to investors while funding climate solutions. They've grown from nothing in 2007 to a $3 trillion market today, reshaping finance.
learn.c1_text: Green bonds are debt instruments where proceeds fund verified environmental projects. Like regular bonds, investors receive interest and principal repayment, typically over 5-20 years. The 'green' label requires third-party verification ensuring funds flow to solar farms, wind projects, or energy storage, not oil pipelines.
learn.c2_text: Green bonds often price 5-15 basis points cheaper than regular bonds due to investor demand for ESG assets. Sovereign issuers like Germany raised €6 billion for renewable expansion. Corporate giants like Apple issued $4.7 billion in green bonds, funding global supplier renewable energy.
learn.c3_text: India issued its first sovereign green bonds in 2023, raising ₹16,000 crore. REC and PFC have issued green masala bonds in foreign currency. Green bond proceeds fund India's solar parks, EV infrastructure, and green hydrogen missions, helping bridge the $10 trillion needed by 2070.
learn.stat1: Global green bond market size: $3 trillion+ cumulative
